region: Monterey County fruit · Woodside, Santa Cruz Mountains, California
about: Thomas Fogarty Winery sits high on Skyline Boulevard above Woodside, in the northern Santa Cruz Mountains, on a 350-acre estate where almost 30 acres are vines and the rest is protected oak and fir forest. It was founded in 1981 by Dr. Thomas Fogarty, the heart surgeon who invented the balloon embolectomy catheter in 1961, together with winemaker Michael Martella. Dr. Fogarty died in December 2025 at 91; Nathan Kandler, who made this wine, is the winery’s general manager and winemaker.

Gewürztraminer is not grown on the mountain estate. Since the winery’s first vintage in 1984 it has come from Monterey County; in recent vintages the source is Scheid’s Viento Vineyard, a gentle east-facing slope on the west side of the Salinas Valley at the foot of the Santa Lucia Mountains, with calcareous shale soils and a cool, windy climate. The winery picks in two passes, riper fruit for exotic perfume and less ripe fruit for crisp acidity and spice, then gives the grapes about a day of skin contact before a long, cool fermentation.

The winery’s notes return to the same hallmarks year after year, lychee, jasmine and candied ginger, with balance between acidity and fruit as the goal. In 2018 the Santa Cruz weekly Good Times singled out this 2015 as a model of the variety, praising its aromatic spice and rich body and suggesting it with turkey and other rich white meats.
facts: Monterey County (Scheid Viento Vineyard in recent vintages)
Two harvest passes, about 24 hours’ skin contact, cool fermentation (recent vintages)
Made from Monterey fruit since the winery’s first vintage, 1984
